Block copolymer (BCP) thin films provide a straightforward means of rapidly and spontaneously generating uniform nanomaterials over macroscopic areas, where polymer architecture reliably encodes the nanoscale structural motif[@b4][@b5]. However, the inherent energy-minimization aspect of self-assembly emphasizes shapes that minimize surface area and maximize symmetry. Self-assembly thus yields a very limited set of morphologies, such as lamellae or hexagonally packed cylinders[@b6][@b7]. Here, we overcome this challenge, and demonstrate how soft self-assembling materials can be manipulated to form a diverse library of previously unreported morphologies. Non-equilibrium morphologies are accessed using a pathway-dependent assembly strategy. Our paradigm relies on the sequential and controlled addition of stimuli, such as solvents, temperature changes, or the introduction of specific chemical entities, to guide the assembly process away from the conventional equilibrium structures. This approach enables the creation of a wide range of morphologies, including branched, hierarchical, and interpenetrating networks, which are not typically observed in equilibrium self-assembly of block copolymers. In a typical pyroelectric detector, incident radiant heat flux is absorbed by the pyroelectric crystal and is converted into heat. Illustration by Davide Bonadonna National Geographic The team, led by Ibrahim and University of Detroit Mercy paleontologist Nizar Ishak, were able to reconstruct a Spinosaurus tail for the first time after unearthing an array of bones at Morocco's Kem Kem fossil beds in 2018. They compared these with other specimens collected from the same site over decades prior. The team found evidence that the Spinosaur had a large paddle-like tail -- something we've seen before in animals like crocodiles and whales, which spend most or all their time underwater. The researchers suggest this would have helped propel it through water at speeds. "Working on this animal was like studying an alien from outer space; nothing like it has ever been described before," said Ibrahim. "This is the tail of a dinosaur that doesn't exist anymore and we know precisely how it was built to swim." The new study comes off the back of another Spinosaurus discovery, in September 2020.

It accuses California politicians of “repeated injuries and usurpations, all having in direct object the establishment of a Tyranny over the Counties of New California”. “After years of over taxation, regulation, and mono party politics the State has succumbed...” it continues. The declaration was made on Monday at an event outside Sacramento's Maclise Room where supporters posed for pictures in front to a “New Cali" poster featuring its flag: white stars set against blue background above two red stripes separated by large golden star centered between them; reminiscent of the California state banner, with New Cal replacing old one. The latest effort follows numerous past attempts aiming at division or separation from this heavily populated coastal US paradise – all unsuccessful thus far due to stringent requirements for such initiatives under Californian law including signaturEs needed totaling 10% electoral participation during most recent gubernatorial contest plus approval via majority vote
